secret.erosion.say: A smooth slab, polished by the wind. On the Martian timescale, this rock was exposed only very recently.
secret.namib.say: Next to it, the face of a huge dune, smooth and steep. It's Namib Dune.
secret.sulfur.say: Your boot cracked a rock, and inside there are yellow crystals! Just like what Curiosity found in 2024.

layer.mapa.name: MAP
layer.mapa.note: Normal view of the terrain. Tap LAYER to switch data layers. Every active layer drains battery (PWR); the MAP does not.
layer.topografia.name: TOPOGRAPHY
layer.topografia.note: Topography. Elevation bands with contour lines. The slope rises toward Mount Sharp. Final version: HiRISE (MRO) elevation models.
layer.minerais.name: MINERALS
layer.minerais.note: Minerals. Clays point to ancient, low-acidity water. Mount Sharp's upper layers are rich in sulfates. Final version: CRISM (MRO) spectra and Curiosity analyses.
layer.terreno.name: TERRAIN
layer.terreno.note: Terrain. Shows where it's risky to step and where to take shelter. Soft sand uses more O₂ and slows you down. Sharp rocks damage the suit.
guide.cruise.title: Radiation in transit
guide.cruise.body: Outside the protection of Earth's magnetic field, radiation is constant. During the cruise to Mars, the RAD instrument aboard Curiosity measured about 1.8 mSv per day.
guide.cruise.lesson: Lesson: have a shielded shelter on the ship and a plan for solar alerts.
guide.cruise.src: Source: NASA/JPL · MSL RAD (Zeitlin et al., Science, 2013)
guide.env.title: The Martian environment
guide.env.body: Gravity is 38% of Earth's and atmospheric pressure is less than 1% of Earth's. A Martian day, a sol, lasts 24h39min. Nights drop to tens of degrees below zero.
guide.env.lesson: Lesson: the suit stays pressurized at all times. Plan the EVA around your oxygen supply.
guide.dust.title: Toxic dust
guide.dust.body: Martian soil contains perchlorates, salts that are toxic to humans. The Phoenix lander detected them in 2008, and Curiosity also found them in Gale Crater.
guide.dust.lesson: Lesson: remove dust from the suit before entering the habitat.
guide.dust.src: Source: NASA/JPL · Phoenix Mars Lander; MSL Curiosity
guide.water.title: Mars once had water
guide.water.body: In 2013, Curiosity drilled the rocks of Yellowknife Bay and found clay minerals. A lake of low-salinity, neutral-pH water once existed there, an environment that could have supported microbial life.
guide.water.lesson: Lesson: fine-grained sedimentary rocks, like mudstones, are the best targets when looking for signs of habitability.
guide.water.src: Source: NASA/JPL-Caltech · MSL (Grotzinger et al., Science, 2014)
guide.sand.title: Soft sand
guide.sand.body: The Bagnold Dunes are active dunes that move with the wind. Curiosity studied them in 2015 and 2016. In 2009, the Spirit rover got stuck in soft soil and never got out.
guide.sand.lesson: Lesson: avoid soft sand and test the ground before moving ahead with cargo.
guide.sand.src: Source: NASA/JPL-Caltech · MSL Curiosity; MER Spirit
guide.power.title: Power and dust
guide.power.body: Opportunity ran on solar power. In June 2018, a dust storm covered the entire planet, and the last contact with the rover was on June 10, 2018. NASA ended the mission in February 2019, after almost 15 years on Mars. Curiosity uses a nuclear power source and kept operating.
guide.power.lesson: Lesson: instruments use power. Plan your EVA battery and keep a reserve for the way back.
guide.power.src: Source: NASA/JPL · Opportunity end of mission (Feb. 2019)
guide.spe.title: Solar particles
guide.spe.body: On the surface, RAD measured an average of about 0.64 mSv per day. A solar particle event can raise the dose quickly. The event's rates and warning time in this game are simulated.
guide.spe.lesson: Lesson: monitor space weather alerts and always keep a shelter a few minutes away.
guide.spe.src: Source: NASA/JPL · MSL RAD (Hassler et al., Science, 2014)
guide.rocks.title: Sharp rocks
guide.rocks.body: In late 2013, the holes and tears in Curiosity's aluminum wheels grew quickly while it crossed terrain with sharp rocks. The team began looking for smoother routes, inspecting the wheels often and testing driving in reverse.
guide.rocks.lesson: Lesson: rocks like these could also cut suits. Go around them when you can and inspect your gear when you return.
guide.box.title: Boxwork formations
guide.box.body: They are networks of ridges in the rock. Groundwater deposited minerals in fractures, and erosion later removed the surrounding rock, leaving the ridges standing out. Curiosity studied these formations in 2025, on Mount Sharp.
guide.box.lesson: Lesson: these ridges record groundwater after the lakes dried up. It's science that can only be done on site.
guide.erosion.title: Erosion clock
guide.erosion.body: The rocks of Yellowknife Bay were exposed about 80 million years ago, when wind eroded the layers covering them. For Martian geology, that is a recent exposure.
guide.erosion.lesson: Lesson: more recently exposed surfaces have spent less time under surface radiation.
guide.namib.title: Namib Dune
guide.namib.body: It is one of the Bagnold Dunes. Its downwind face slopes about 28° and stands about 5 m tall. Orbital images show these dunes advance up to about 1 m per Earth year.
guide.namib.lesson: Lesson: dunes move. Update your route with recent images.
guide.sulfur.title: Sulfur crystals
guide.sulfur.body: On May 30, 2024 (sol 4,200), Curiosity drove over a rock in the Gediz Vallis channel, nicknamed Convict Lake, and cracked it open. Inside were yellow crystals of pure sulfur, identified by the APXS instrument. It was the first time pure sulfur was found on Mars.
guide.sulfur.lesson: Lesson: discoveries can happen by chance. Record everything, even what turns up under your feet.
diary.cruise: Day 112 of the trip. The alarm went off before dawn and we spent hours squeezed into the shelter. Outside, the Sun never stops. In here, I learned that fear can also be measured in mSv.
diary.env: Sol 1. I took my first step and almost jumped too high: here I weigh a little over a third of what I weighed at home. The sky is the color of caramel, and the silence is absolute. Without the suit, I wouldn't last a minute.
diary.dust: Keli said over the radio: "Clean your suit before coming in." This red dust is beautiful, but it's poison.
diary.water: I touched a rock that was once mud at the bottom of a lake. Real water, calm, with neutral pH. Maybe something lived here. I stood still for a while, just looking.
diary.erosion: The wind took millions of years to uncover this slab. For Mars, that's yesterday. I'm the first person to touch it.
diary.sand: The dunes look soft, but Spirit got stuck in sand like this and never got out. Tatu complained every meter. We went around.
diary.namib: A wall of dark sand as tall as a house. And it moves: up to a meter a year. Today's map won't work tomorrow.
diary.power: My suit battery dropped to 30%. I remembered Opportunity, which fell asleep in a dust storm and never woke up. I turned off the instruments and kept walking.
diary.spe: Alert: a solar flare. Forty-five minutes to take cover. I ran like never before inside a suit. Reaching the shelter was the best hug of my life.
diary.rocks: The stones here are knives. Rocks like these punched holes in Curiosity's wheels. Today they scraped my suit. A small cut, but the air is unforgiving.
diary.sulfur: I stepped on a rock and it broke. Inside, yellow crystals, shining. Curiosity found something like this by chance, in 2024. Mars keeps surprises under our feet.
diary.box: I made it. Crossing ridges, like the walls of a stone honeycomb. Water flowed underground long after the lakes dried up. I stored the sample with shaking hands.

teaser.0.line0: Since the beginning, we have looked at the sky and wondered what lay beyond.
teaser.0.line1: For millennia, it was only a dream.
teaser.0.line2: Until, one day, we decided to go.
teaser.1.line0: Before any astronaut, there was him.
teaser.1.line1: A chimpanzee named Ham, aboard a Mercury capsule.
teaser.1.line2: He went up, faced the unknown... and came back alive.
teaser.2.line0: Alan Shepard broke the barrier and went to space.
teaser.2.line1: “Godspeed, John Glenn.” With those words, Glenn circled the Earth three times.
teaser.2.line2: Years later, Sally Ride showed that space belonged to everyone.
teaser.3.line0: Millions of people in silence. Neil Armstrong climbs down the ladder.
teaser.3.line1: “That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.”
teaser.3.line2: Beside him, Buzz Aldrin. In orbit, Michael Collins waiting for them.
teaser.4.line2: Lovell, Swigert and Haise had a single mission: survive.
teaser.5.line0: For decades, we sent our eyes where we could not yet go.
teaser.5.line2: Every piece of data was a promise: one day, someone would come.
teaser.6.line0: Half a century later, we traveled to the Moon again.
teaser.6.line1: The Artemis II crew (Wiseman, Glover, Koch and Hansen) flew around its far side and looked ahead.
teaser.6.line2: Toward a red dot in the sky.

travel.0: The ship leaves Earth orbit bound for Mars. The crossing takes about 7 months, the same time Perseverance took.
travel.1: Far from Earth's magnetic field, radiation is constant. Curiosity measured about 1.8 mSv per day on this route.
travel.2: Solar storm alert! Everyone to the shelter, the most heavily shielded area of the ship.
travel.3: Radiation in transit: have a shielded shelter and a plan for solar alerts.
travel.4: Every month, messages to Earth take longer. Near Mars, real-time conversation is no longer possible.
travel.5: Mars in sight. Beginning entry, descent and landing. Hold on.
landing.title: 7 MINUTES OF TERROR
landing.note: The signal takes minutes to reach Earth. No one can step in in time: everything is automatic.
brief.ykb.name: Yellowknife Bay
brief.ykb.what: A shallow depression near Curiosity's landing site: the rover had driven about 680 m when it got there. Fine-grained, layered rocks that formed at the bottom of an ancient lake are exposed there.
brief.ykb.why: It was the first rock Curiosity drilled, in 2013. We are going to find out whether Gale once had water able to support microbial life.
brief.ykb.look: Look for smooth rock, cracked into slabs, with light-colored veins: that is mudstone.
brief.bag.name: Bagnold Dunes
brief.bag.what: A field of dark dunes along the northwest base of Mount Sharp. It is named after Ralph Bagnold, a British engineer who studied how wind shapes dunes on Earth.
brief.bag.why: They are active dunes: the wind still moves them. In 2015 and 2016, Curiosity made the first close-up visit to active dunes beyond Earth there. The way to Mount Sharp goes through them.
brief.bag.look: Dark sand with ripples. It is soft: go around it when you can.
brief.bag.src: NASA/JPL-Caltech · MSL Curiosity, Bagnold Dunes campaign (2015–2016)
brief.box.name: Boxwork Formations
brief.box.what: Networks of crisscrossing ridges on the slope of Mount Sharp, visible even from orbit. Groundwater left minerals in the rock's fractures, and erosion removed the rest.
brief.box.why: They show that water still flowed underground after the lakes dried up, which may have extended the time Gale was habitable. Curiosity reached them in 2025.
brief.box.look: Ridges in relief forming "boxes". The mission sample is collected there.
brief.home.name: Habitat
brief.home.what: The mission base, where the crew lives and works.
brief.home.why: The sample has to come back to be analyzed and logged. Completing the Field Guide is the mission's final goal.
brief.home.look: Pressurized structure at the original landing site (Bradbury Landing).
brief.shel.name: Shelter
brief.shel.what: A solar particle event is on its way: high-energy protons launched by the Sun.
brief.shel.why: The walls of the habitat and the pressurized rover reduce the dose. Outside, the suit offers little protection.
brief.shel.look: Get close to the rover or the habitat and press {A} to enter.
brief.shel.src: NASA/JPL · MSL RAD (Hassler et al., Science, 2014)

eva.intro.0: Touchdown confirmed in Gale Crater. Welcome to Mars, Dr. Selari.
eva.intro.1: There are four of us: I stay at the habitat, Dr. Natan Jonas looks after our health, and Eng. Rossi Brook is at the pressurized rover, near the dunes. Talk to us with {A}.
eva.intro.2: Gravity here is 38% of Earth's, and the pressure is less than 1% of Earth's. Without a suit, there is no survival.
eva.intro.3: The Martian environment: a sol lasts 24h39min. Today's EVA has oxygen for about 8 hours.
eva.intro.4: The soil has perchlorates, toxic salts. Clean your suit before entering the habitat.
eva.intro.5: Toxic dust: remove dust from the suit before going in.
eva.intro.6: Your map already has the topography layer. Use LAYER to switch. Slopes and rocks block the way.
eva.intro.7: The suit has three reserves: O₂, battery (PWR) and integrity (SUIT). Data layers drain battery. The habitat and the rover restore everything.
eva.intro.8: First target: Yellowknife Bay. Tatu, our cargo rover, will lead the way. Follow Tatu: if you fall behind, it waits for you.
eva.intro.9: If you have time left, explore off the route. Keep an eye out for glints on the ground.
eva.ykb.0: Yellowknife Bay. Fine-grained rock, in layers... it's a mudstone.
eva.ykb.1: This is where Curiosity drilled in 2013. It found clay minerals: a lake of low-salinity water once existed here.
eva.ykb.2: Mars once had water, in an environment that could have supported microbial life.
eva.ykb.4: Next target: Bagnold Dunes. Watch out for the sand.
eva.bag.0: Bagnold Dunes. Active dunes: the wind still moves them today.
eva.bag.1: In 2009, the Spirit rover got stuck in soft soil and never got out. Don't repeat that mistake.
eva.bag.2: Soft sand: avoid it and test the ground before moving ahead with cargo.
eva.bag.3: Soil sensor ready. TERRAIN layer unlocked: it shows sand, slopes and shelters.
eva.bag.4: Final target: the boxwork formations, up the slope of Mount Sharp.
eva.box.0: There they are. Crossing ridges, like the walls of a box.
eva.box.1: Boxwork formations. Groundwater deposited minerals in fractures. Erosion left the ridges standing out.
eva.box.2: Boxwork: a record of groundwater, studied by Curiosity in 2025.
eva.box.4: Excellent work. Head back to the habitat. The pressurized rover can refill your O₂ on the way.
poi.home.name: Habitat
poi.rover.name: Pressurized rover
crew.commander.say0: Remember: oxygen decides the route, not curiosity.
crew.commander.say1: Sample on board? Then head back to the habitat, no detours.
crew.doctor.say0: Before going into the habitat, clean your suit at the cleaning point right next to me: brush and electrostatic panel. The dust has perchlorates, which are toxic.
crew.engineer.say0: The pressurized rover refills O₂, battery and suit. Use it whenever you pass by.
crew.engineer.say1: On the way to the boxwork there are sharp rocks. Rocks like these punched holes in Curiosity's wheels in 2013.
secret.found: {title}: extra entry logged in the Guide.
ending.l0: Back at the habitat, Ana writes the last page of the Guide and sends it to Earth.
ending.l1: “You will read this a few years from now. Everything I learned is in these pages: the lake, the sand, the Sun, the rocks.”
ending.l2: “I didn't get this far alone. The robots came first and marked the way.”

eva.dusk.warn: It is {time} and the sun is about to set. The temperature will drop to nearly −70 °C. Head back to the habitat.
eva.fail.night: Night fell while you were outside. The Tatu brought you back to the habitat, but your suit barely held against the cold.
eva.tatu.off: Battery depleted. The Tatu went into hibernation and shut down its instruments. Only the normal view works.
eva.tatu.noLayer: TATU OUT OF POWER: INSTRUMENTS OFF
eva.storm.warn: A dust storm is closing in from the south. With the sky shut, the Tatu's panels barely generate power. Switch off the layers you don't need and head back to the habitat.
eva.devil.first: The dust devil rolled right over me and swept the dust off my panels! Charging got better.
eva.devil.passed: DUST DEVIL PASSED BY THE TATU
eva.spe.0: Alert! Satellites detected a solar flare. The particles arrive in about 45 minutes.
eva.spe.1: Get to a shelter: the pressurized rover, near the dunes, or the habitat. Tatu will lead you to the nearest one.
eva.spe.2: Get close to a shelter and press {A} to go in. Crew nearby go in too and only come out when the event is over. Press {A} again to go out.
eva.spe.hit: The particles are here and you are outside! They also hit electronics: in 2003, a solar storm damaged the MARIE instrument on the Mars Odyssey orbiter. Your data layers will fail out here.
eva.spe.dose: Event dose: {dose}. That already equals about {days} days on the surface of Mars, by RAD's average (0.64 mSv per day).
eva.spe.limit: You are past 50 mSv: more than 8% of a NASA astronaut's career limit of 600 mSv. The risk is long term, mainly cancer. Get to a shelter now!
eva.spe.abort: Dose above this mission's limit. EVA aborted: Tatu will take you to the habitat now.
eva.spe.evac: Evacuation: Tatu rushes you to the habitat, the best-shielded shelter at the base.
eva.spe.end: Event over. Dose received during the alert: {dose}, about {days} days on the surface.
eva.spe.guide: Solar particles: monitor alerts and keep a shelter a few minutes away.
eva.spe.next: Final target: the boxwork formations, up the slope of Mount Sharp.
eva.clean.ask: Your suit is still covered in perchlorate dust. Are you sure you want to go into the habitat without cleaning it?
eva.spe.endLow: Event over. Dose received during the alert: {dose}, less than one day on the surface. The shelter worked.
eva.return.warn: Point of return! You have {o2}% of O₂ and need about {need}% to reach shelter. Head back now.
eva.return.obj: POINT OF RETURN: HEAD BACK TO SHELTER
eva.fail.o2: O₂ depleted. EVA aborted: the Tatu brought you back to the habitat.
eva.fail.suit: Suit integrity lost. EVA aborted: Tatu brought you back to the habitat.
eva.rocks.selari: Sharp rocks! I felt my suit scrape.
eva.rocks.hastor: In 2013, rocks like these punched holes in Curiosity's aluminum wheels. With the suit below 50%, it starts leaking O₂.
eva.rocks.guide: Sharp rocks: go around them when you can. The habitat and the rover repair the suit.
eva.wheels.hit: Spiky rocks! They cut the wheels. Worn wheels make the Tatu use more battery.
eva.solar.warn1: Alert! Satellites detected a solar flare. The particles arrive in about 45 minutes.
eva.solar.warn2: Get to a shelter: the pressurized rover or the habitat. The arrow points to the nearest one.
eva.solar.end: Event over. Dose received during the alert: {dose}.
